grade_rationale.text: Every verified peoples row names the Russians: Ralston's Russian peasants, and a variant from the Kursk Government.
Afanasyev records the peasants' Morozko, a little old man with a long grey beard, and the Christmas Eve call inviting Frost to eat kissel or kutya.
Afanasyev's 1865 and 1868 volumes (Moroz-Treskun in the red-hot bath) are counted as one source.

Ralston's paragraph on Moroz as a living personage, the kissel custom, the Tcheremisses and the ice hut cites Afanasyev (P.V.S. i. 318-19), and his Kursk variant cites Afanasief IV. No 42. b, so those passages are not independent of Afanasyev.
Ralston's translated tale of the stepdaughter left under the pine for Frost cites no Afanasyev on the pages opened, so for that tale he counts as a second, independent source.
One people with two independent sources gives the grade regional.
